## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`requirement_proven` must get its empty-list guard back before merge, because the rewritten check reports a requirement with no criteria as proven.

## Changes
The pull request rewrites `requirement_proven` in `app/proof.py` to count proven criteria instead of using `all()`, and adds a `reviewed_batch` helper plus a `REVIEW_HINT` constant. It also adds `tests/test_proof.py` covering both functions.

## Critical
- app/proof.py:3 — correctness — Restore the non-empty guard and all() check in requirement_proven — `requirement_proven([])` now returns `True` because `0 == len([])`; the base code returned `False` through `bool(criteria) and all(...)`. Separately, `[{"proven": None}]` now raises `TypeError` in the `sum(...)` on line 2, where the base code returned `False`. — A requirement with no criteria is reported as proven, and a criterion with a null `proven` value crashes the check instead of failing it. — Fix: Return `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)` and extend `test_requirement_with_evidence` in `tests/test_proof.py` with the empty-list case.
